subject: Anatomy
exp: Most cardiac venous blood drains into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.

subject: Biochemistry
q: Normal arterial blood pH is approximately:
exp: Arterial pH is tightly maintained at 7.35-7.45, averaging 7.40.
optExp: Neutral pH — outside biological range for blood.

subject: Embryology
q: Which germ layer gives rise to the nervous system?
exp: Neural tube derived from ectoderm forms the CNS; neural crest cells form much of PNS.

subject: Genetics
q: How many chromosomes are in a normal human somatic cell?
exp: Human somatic cells are diploid with 46 chromosomes (22 autosome pairs + XX/XY).
optExp: Only autosomes counted; sex chromosomes excluded incorrectly.

subject: Histology
q: Which cell breaks down bone tissue?
exp: Osteoclasts are large multinucleated cells (from monocyte lineage) that resorb bone via H⁺ and proteases.
optExp: Fibroblasts make collagen in connective tissue.

subject: Immunology
q: The first antibody produced in a primary immune response is:
exp: IgM is the first antibody produced in response to a new antigen (primary response).

subject: Pathology
q: A malignant tumour of mesenchymal origin is a:
exp: Sarcomas arise from mesenchymal tissue (bone, muscle, fat, fibrous, blood vessels). Carcinomas are epithelial.

subject: Pharmacology
q: CYP450 enzymes are mainly found in the:
exp: CYP450 enzymes are most concentrated in hepatocyte smooth ER, performing most of Phase I drug metabolism.
optExp: Brain has some CYPs but minor.

subject: Physiology
q: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is approximately:
exp: Resting Vm is around −70 mV, established by Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and K⁺ leak channels.
optExp: +40 mV is the peak of the AP.
